title: Narrative of the Life of Frederick Douglass, an American Slave
short: Narrative of the Life of Frederick Douglass
author: Frederick Douglass
blurb: Frederick Douglass recounts his childhood in Talbot County, Maryland, learning to read in Baltimore, his fight with Covey, and his escape north to freedom in New Bedford.

title: Incidents in the Life of a Slave Girl
short: Incidents in the Life of a Slave Girl
author: Harriet Jacobs
blurb: Writing as Linda Brent, the author tells of her master's persecution, seven years hidden in a cramped garret, her escape north, and freedom at last for herself and her children.

title: Twelve Years a Slave: Narrative of Solomon Northup, a Citizen of New-York, Kidnapped in Washington City in 1841, and Rescued in 1853, from a Cotton Plantation near the Red River, in Louisiana
author: Solomon Northup
blurb: Solomon Northup, a free citizen of New York, was kidnapped in Washington in 1841 and held twelve years on Louisiana plantations near the Red River until his rescue in 1853.

title: The Interesting Narrative of the Life of Olaudah Equiano, or Gustavus Vassa, the African
short: The Interesting Narrative of Olaudah Equiano
author: Olaudah Equiano
blurb: Equiano tells of his childhood in Eboe, his kidnapping and passage on a slave ship, years as an enslaved seaman, how he bought his freedom, and his later travels.

title: Running a Thousand Miles for Freedom; or, The Escape of William and Ellen Craft from Slavery
short: Running a Thousand Miles for Freedom
author: William and Ellen Craft
blurb: William and Ellen Craft escaped from slavery in Georgia in December 1848, Ellen disguised as an invalid gentleman with William as her slave, and later fled to England.

title: The History of Mary Prince, a West Indian Slave
author: Mary Prince
blurb: Mary Prince tells of her enslavement in Bermuda, at the salt ponds of Turk's Island and in Antigua, and of leaving her owners' household in London.

title: Narrative of Sojourner Truth
author: Sojourner Truth
blurb: Dictated by Sojourner Truth, the narrative follows Isabella from slavery in Ulster County, New York, through her escape, her lawsuit to recover her son, and her preaching travels.

title: My Bondage and My Freedom
author: Frederick Douglass
blurb: Douglass retells his Maryland childhood, enslavement and escape, then follows his life as an abolitionist lecturer, his twenty-one months in Great Britain, and his newspaper work, with speeches appended.

title: Up from Slavery: An Autobiography
author: Booker T. Washington
blurb: Booker T. Washington tells of his birth in slavery in Franklin County, Virginia, his schooling at Hampton, and his work building Tuskegee Institute in Alabama.

title: Narrative of William W. Brown, a Fugitive Slave
author: William Wells Brown
blurb: William Wells Brown describes slavery in Kentucky and Missouri, being hired out to a slave trader on the Mississippi, and his escape to Ohio, where a Quaker named him.

title: Narrative of the Life and Adventures of Henry Bibb, an American Slave
short: The Life and Adventures of Henry Bibb
author: Henry Bibb
blurb: Henry Bibb recounts slavery in Kentucky, his escapes and returns to rescue his wife and child, their sale together to the far South, and his life as a free lecturer.

title: The Fugitive Blacksmith; or, Events in the History of James W. C. Pennington, Pastor of a Presbyterian Church, New York, Formerly a Slave in the State of Maryland, United States
author: James W. C. Pennington
blurb: James W. C. Pennington, a blacksmith enslaved on Maryland's eastern shore, tells of his flight north, his capture and escape, Quaker friends in Pennsylvania, and his religious calling.

title: Behind the Scenes; or, Thirty Years a Slave, and Four Years in the White House
author: Elizabeth Keckley
blurb: Elizabeth Keckley recounts her girlhood in slavery in Virginia, buying freedom for herself and her son in St. Louis, and her years as Mrs. Lincoln's dressmaker and friend in Washington.

title: A Narrative of the Life and Adventures of Venture, a Native of Africa, but Resident above Sixty Years in the United States of America
short: The Life and Adventures of Venture
author: Venture Smith
blurb: Venture, son of a prince in Guinea, describes his capture as a child, his enslavement in New York and Connecticut, and buying freedom for himself and his family.

title: Narrative of the Life of Moses Grandy, Late a Slave in the United States of America
short: Narrative of the Life of Moses Grandy
author: Moses Grandy
blurb: Moses Grandy of Camden County, North Carolina, a canal boatman, tells how he paid for his freedom three times over before working to redeem his wife and children.

title: The Narrative of Lunsford Lane, Formerly of Raleigh, N.C., Embracing an Account of His Early Life, the Redemption by Purchase of Himself and Family from Slavery, and His Banishment from the Place of His Birth for the Crime of Wearing a Colored Skin
author: Lunsford Lane
blurb: Lunsford Lane of Raleigh, North Carolina, bought his freedom with money earned selling tobacco, then was banished from the state while trying to buy his wife and children.

title: Harriet, the Moses of Her People
short: Harriet, the Moses of Her People
author: Sarah H. Bradford
blurb: Sarah Bradford tells how Harriet Tubman escaped slavery in Maryland, returned south again and again to lead others out, and served the Union army as scout and nurse.

title: Twenty-Two Years a Slave, and Forty Years a Freeman; Embracing a Correspondence of Several Years, While President of Wilberforce Colony, London, Canada West
author: Austin Steward
blurb: Austin Steward recalls slavery on a Virginia plantation and in New York, his freedom and business life in Rochester, and his years leading the Wilberforce colony in Canada.

title: Thirty Years a Slave: From Bondage to Freedom; The Institution of Slavery as Seen on the Plantation and in the Home of the Planter
author: Louis Hughes
blurb: Louis Hughes, sold in Richmond as a boy, describes slavery on a Mississippi plantation and in Memphis, repeated escape attempts, his freedom during the war, and later life in Milwaukee.

title: A Slave Girl's Story: Being an Autobiography of Kate Drumgoold
author: Kate Drumgoold
blurb: Kate Drumgoold recalls a Virginia childhood in slavery, her mother's sale during the war and return, and her own schooling and years as a teacher.

title: Memories of Childhood's Slavery Days
author: Annie L. Burton
blurb: Annie L. Burton remembers her childhood on a plantation near Clayton, Alabama, during the Civil War and her life after freedom, followed by essays, poems and hymns.

title: From the Darkness Cometh the Light; or, Struggles for Freedom
short: From the Darkness Cometh the Light
author: Lucy A. Delaney
blurb: Lucy A. Delaney tells how her mother, a free woman kidnapped from Illinois into slavery, won her freedom in court and then sued in St. Louis to free her daughter.

title: The Story of Mattie J. Jackson; Her Parentage—Experience of Eighteen Years in Slavery—Incidents during the War—Her Escape from Slavery
short: The Story of Mattie J. Jackson
author: Mattie J. Jackson
blurb: Mattie J. Jackson describes slavery in St. Louis during the Civil War, her family's sales and escape attempts, and her own escape to freedom in Indianapolis.

title: Memoir of Old Elizabeth, a Coloured Woman
author: Old Elizabeth
blurb: Born a slave in Maryland in 1766, Elizabeth tells of her religious awakening, her freedom, and her many years travelling as a preacher before settling in Philadelphia.

title: A Narrative of the Life of Rev. Noah Davis, a Colored Man
short: The Life of Rev. Noah Davis
author: Noah Davis
blurb: Noah Davis, born a slave in Virginia, tells how he became a Baptist preacher, bought his own freedom, and worked in Baltimore to buy his wife and children.

title: Narrative of the Life of J. D. Green, a Runaway Slave, from Kentucky, Containing an Account of His Three Escapes, in 1839, 1846, and 1848
short: Narrative of the Life of J. D. Green
author: J. D. Green
blurb: J. D. Green tells of slavery in Maryland and his three escapes, in 1839, 1846 and 1848, the last of which brought him to freedom in Canada.

title: The Confessions of Nat Turner, the Leader of the Late Insurrections in Southampton, Va.
author: Nat Turner
blurb: In his cell, Nat Turner tells Thomas R. Gray of his visions and of the 1831 revolt he led in Southampton, Virginia; Gray adds the trial and court lists.

title: Wonderful Adventures of Mrs. Seacole in Many Lands
author: Mary Seacole
blurb: Mary Seacole of Kingston, Jamaica, tells of fighting cholera in Panama and of her British Hotel near Balaclava, where she fed and nursed soldiers during the Crimean War.

title: The Underground Rail Road: A Record of Facts, Authentic Narratives, Letters, &c.
author: William Still
blurb: William Still, chairman of Philadelphia's Acting Vigilance Committee, records the escapes of hundreds of fugitives it aided, with their letters, advertisements for runaways, and sketches of abolitionist helpers.

title: The Colored Cadet at West Point: Autobiography of Lieut. Henry Ossian Flipper, U.S.A., First Graduate of Color from the U.S. Military Academy
short: The Colored Cadet at West Point
author: Henry Ossian Flipper
blurb: Henry O. Flipper, born a slave in Georgia, recounts his four years of ostracism at West Point and his graduation in 1877 as the academy's first graduate of color.

title: Life and Times of Frederick Douglass, Written by Himself: His Early Life as a Slave, His Escape from Bondage, and His Complete History to the Present Time
short: Life and Times of Frederick Douglass
author: Frederick Douglass
blurb: Douglass’s third autobiography retells his slavery and escape, then follows the antislavery years, John Brown, recruiting Black regiments, Lincoln, Reconstruction and his public offices to 1881.

title: A Negro Explorer at the North Pole
short: A Negro Explorer at the North Pole
author: Matthew A. Henson
blurb: Matthew Henson, who served on Robert E. Peary's Arctic expeditions from 1891, describes the 1908–09 sledge journey across the polar sea that reached the North Pole.

title: Slave Narratives: A Folk History of Slavery in the United States from Interviews with Former Slaves, Florida Narratives
author: Federal Writers' Project
blurb: Interviews with formerly enslaved people in Florida, recorded 1936–38 by the Federal Writers' Project, many by its Negro Writers' Unit, in Jacksonville, Tampa, Miami and smaller towns across the state.

title: Slave Narratives: A Folk History of Slavery in the United States from Interviews with Former Slaves, Georgia Narratives, Part 1
author: Federal Writers' Project
blurb: Interviews, Adams to Furr, with formerly enslaved people in Georgia, recorded 1936–38 by the Federal Writers' Project in Athens, Augusta, Atlanta, Columbus, Macon and elsewhere, with folklore and conjure tales.

title: Slave Narratives: A Folk History of Slavery in the United States from Interviews with Former Slaves, Kentucky Narratives
author: Federal Writers' Project
blurb: Interviews with formerly enslaved people in Kentucky, recorded 1936–38 by the Federal Writers' Project, followed by county reports on local slavery, tales, songs, a bill of sale and a will.

title: Slave Narratives: A Folk History of Slavery in the United States from Interviews with Former Slaves, Maryland Narratives
author: Federal Writers' Project
blurb: Twenty-two interviews with formerly enslaved people in Maryland, recorded 1936–38 by the Federal Writers' Project, most in Baltimore, telling of plantation work, sales, escapes, the Civil War and freedom.

title: Slave Narratives: A Folk History of Slavery in the United States from Interviews with Former Slaves, Mississippi Narratives
author: Federal Writers' Project
blurb: Twenty-six interviews with formerly enslaved people in Mississippi, recorded 1936–38 by the Federal Writers' Project, among them James Lucas, who was once owned by Jefferson Davis.

title: Slave Narratives: A Folk History of Slavery in the United States from Interviews with Former Slaves, North Carolina Narratives, Part 1
author: Federal Writers' Project
blurb: Eighty-nine interviews, Adams to Hunter, with formerly enslaved people in North Carolina, recorded 1936–38 by the Federal Writers' Project, mostly around Raleigh, Durham, Wilmington and Asheville.

title: Slave Narratives: A Folk History of Slavery in the United States from Interviews with Former Slaves, South Carolina Narratives, Part 1
author: Federal Writers' Project
blurb: Eighty-nine interviews, Abrams to Durant, with formerly enslaved people in South Carolina, recorded 1936–38 by the Federal Writers' Project, from Winnsboro, Union and Newberry to Marion and the Georgetown coast.

title: Slave Narratives: A Folk History of Slavery in the United States from Interviews with Former Slaves, Tennessee Narratives
author: Federal Writers' Project
blurb: Twenty-six interviews with formerly enslaved people in Tennessee, recorded 1936–38 by the Federal Writers' Project, most in Nashville and a few in Knoxville, with spirituals and memories of freedom.

title: Slave Narratives: A Folk History of Slavery in the United States from Interviews with Former Slaves, Texas Narratives, Part 1
author: Federal Writers' Project
blurb: Eighty-seven interviews, Adams to Duhon, with formerly enslaved people in Texas, recorded 1936–38 by the Federal Writers' Project, recalling slavery across the South, the Civil War and freedom in Texas.

title: Slave Narratives: A Folk History of Slavery in the United States from Interviews with Former Slaves, Virginia Narratives
author: Federal Writers' Project
blurb: Fourteen interviews with formerly enslaved people in Virginia, recorded 1936–38 by the Federal Writers' Project in Petersburg, Norfolk, Portsmouth and the Tidewater, with songs, folk beliefs and wartime memories.

title: The Past and the Present Condition, and the Destiny, of the Colored Race: A Discourse Delivered at the Fifteenth Anniversary of the Female Benevolent Society of Troy, N.Y., Feb. 14, 1848
short: The Destiny of the Colored Race
author: Henry Highland Garnet
blurb: Henry Highland Garnet’s 1848 discourse at Troy, New York, surveying the African past, the present condition of the colored race under slavery and prejudice, and its destiny in America.

title: Life and Public Services of Martin R. Delany, Sub-Assistant Commissioner Bureau Relief of Refugees, Freedmen, and of Abandoned Lands, and Late Major 104th U.S. Colored Troops
short: Life and Public Services of Martin R. Delany
author: Frank A. Rollin
blurb: Frances Rollin’s life of Martin R. Delany: physician, editor, emigrationist, Niger Valley explorer, first Black major in the Union army, Freedmen’s Bureau agent; with his political writings.

title: A Review of Hoffman's Race Traits and Tendencies of the American Negro
short: A Review of Hoffman's Race Traits
author: Kelly Miller
blurb: Kelly Miller answers, chapter by chapter, the insurance statistician Frederick Hoffman’s claim that the American Negro was dying out through inborn race traits, using Hoffman’s own figures.

title: Right on the Scaffold, or The Martyrs of 1822
author: Archibald H. Grimké
blurb: Archibald Grimké’s account of Denmark Vesey’s planned slave rising in Charleston in 1822, its betrayal, the trials, and the hanging of Vesey and his companions.

title: John Brown
author: W. E. B. Du Bois
blurb: Du Bois’s life of John Brown, told from the side of the Black Americans he lived and worked among: Kansas, the great plan, Harper’s Ferry, the trial and its legacy.

title: The Crisis: A Record of the Darker Races, Volume One, Number One, November 1910
author: W. E. B. Du Bois (ed.)
blurb: The first number of the NAACP’s monthly, edited by W. E. B. Du Bois: news along the color line, opinion, editorials, Moorfield Storey on Brownsville, a reading list, advertisements.

title: The Negro and the Nation
author: Hubert H. Harrison
blurb: Hubert Harrison’s first book: six articles from the socialist and radical press, 1912–1917, on the Black man’s burden, socialism and the Negro, conservatism, and the newspapers’ treatment of the race.

title: When Africa Awakes: The "Inside Story" of the Stirrings and Strivings of the New Negro in the Western World
author: Hubert H. Harrison
blurb: Hubert Harrison’s editorials and articles of 1917–1920 on the Liberty League, lynching, the war, the New Negro in politics, race-first radicalism, Africa and the colonial world, with book reviews.

title: Walker's Appeal, with a Brief Sketch of His Life; and also Garnet's Address to the Slaves of the United States of America
author: David Walker
blurb: David Walker's 1829 Appeal urges the colored citizens of the world to resist slavery; Henry Highland Garnet adds a sketch of Walker's life and his 1843 Address to the Slaves.

title: The Condition, Elevation, Emigration, and Destiny of the Colored People of the United States
short: The Condition of the Colored People
author: Martin Robison Delany
blurb: Martin R. Delany surveys the condition and achievements of free colored Americans, condemns the colonization of Liberia, and argues for emigration to Central and South America and the West Indies.

title: Collected Articles of Frederick Douglass
author: Frederick Douglass
blurb: Two magazine articles by Frederick Douglass: "My Escape from Slavery" (1881), telling how he fled Maryland disguised as a sailor, and "Reconstruction" (1866), urging Congress to enfranchise the freedmen.

title: John Brown: An Address at the Fourteenth Anniversary of Storer College
author: Frederick Douglass
blurb: Frederick Douglass, speaking at Harper's Ferry in 1881, recalls his friendship with John Brown, recounts the 1859 raid, and argues that Brown began the war that ended slavery.

title: Southern Horrors: Lynch Law in All Its Phases
author: Ida B. Wells
blurb: Ida B. Wells's 1892 pamphlet, written after a mob destroyed her Memphis newspaper, examines the charge of rape used to excuse lynching and urges self-help, boycott and emigration.

title: The Red Record: Tabulated Statistics and Alleged Causes of Lynching in the United States
author: Ida B. Wells
blurb: Ida B. Wells's 1895 record of lynchings in the United States, drawn from the Chicago Tribune's figures for 1892–1894, with case histories, her dispute with Frances Willard, and proposed remedies.

title: The Conservation of Races
author: W. E. B. Du Bois
blurb: Du Bois's 1897 paper for the American Negro Academy argues that each race has a message for humanity and that Black Americans should keep their race identity.

title: The Future of the American Negro
short: The Future of the American Negro
author: Booker T. Washington
blurb: Booker T. Washington argues that industrial education is the way forward for Black Americans in the South, describing Tuskegee's work and discussing politics, the franchise and lynching.

title: Mob Rule in New Orleans: Robert Charles and His Fight to Death, the Story of His Life, Burning Human Beings Alive, Other Lynching Statistics
author: Ida B. Wells
blurb: Ida B. Wells's account of the New Orleans riot of July 1900, when Robert Charles fought off a police assault and mobs attacked Black residents, with lynching statistics.

title: The Souls of Black Folk
author: W. E. B. Du Bois
blurb: Du Bois's essays on the color line and double consciousness, the Freedmen's Bureau, Booker T. Washington, the Black Belt, Black faith and education, and the Sorrow Songs.

title: The Negro Problem: A Series of Articles by Representative American Negroes of To-day
author: Booker T. Washington, W. E. B. Du Bois, et al.
blurb: Seven essays on the condition and future of Black Americans: Washington on industrial education, Du Bois's "The Talented Tenth", Chesnutt on disfranchisement, and pieces by Smith, Kealing, Dunbar and Fortune.

title: Masterpieces of Negro Eloquence: The Best Speeches Delivered by the Negro from the Days of Slavery to the Present Time
author: Alice Moore Dunbar (ed.)
blurb: Alice Moore Dunbar's anthology of fifty-one speeches by Black orators from 1818 to 1913, among them Frederick Douglass, Frances Harper, Henry Highland Garnet, Alexander Crummell and Booker T. Washington.

title: Darkwater: Voices from Within the Veil
author: W. E. B. Du Bois
blurb: Du Bois's essays on his own life, white supremacy, Africa and empire, work and wealth, democracy, women and children, alternating with poems, prayers and parables.

title: Self-Determining Haiti
author: James Weldon Johnson
blurb: James Weldon Johnson's four 1920 articles for The Nation report on the American occupation of Haiti, its killings, forced labor and financial control, with the treaty and other documents.

title: Aesop's Fables
author: Aesop
blurb: Over three hundred fables in Townsend’s 1867 translation, from the Wolf and the Lamb to the Fox and the Grapes, with his life of the slave storyteller Aesop.

title: An Account of Egypt
author: Herodotus
blurb: Book II of Herodotus’s Histories, the Greek traveller’s account of Egypt in the fifth century BC: the Nile, its gods, animals and customs, and the history of its kings.

title: Oroonoko; or, The Royal Slave
author: Aphra Behn
blurb: Aphra Behn's 1688 tale of Oroonoko, an African prince of Coramantien sold into slavery in Surinam with his beloved Imoinda, and the revolt he leads; with Montague Summers's notes.

title: A Narrative of the Most Remarkable Particulars in the Life of James Albert Ukawsaw Gronniosaw, an African Prince, as Related by Himself
short: The Life of James Albert Ukawsaw Gronniosaw
author: James Albert Ukawsaw Gronniosaw
blurb: Dictated in old age: a Bornu prince is sold into slavery on the Guinea coast, freed in New York, and lives poor but devout in England.

title: Letters of the Late Ignatius Sancho, an African, to Which Are Prefixed Memoirs of His Life
author: Ignatius Sancho
blurb: Letters of Ignatius Sancho, born on a slave ship and later a London grocer, composer and man of letters, written to friends from 1768 to 1780, with a memoir.

title: The Ruins; or, Meditation on the Revolutions of Empires, and the Law of Nature
author: C. F. Volney
blurb: Volney's 1791 meditation among the ruins of Palmyra on why empires fall, holding that Black Ethiopians first discovered the arts and sciences and founded religion; with The Law of Nature.

title: Antar, a Bedoueen Romance
author: Anonymous
blurb: First part of the Arabian romance of Antar, son of an Arab chief and an enslaved Black woman, who rises by valour and poetry, seeking his cousin Ibla.

title: The Hour and the Man: An Historical Romance
author: Harriet Martineau
blurb: Harriet Martineau's 1841 novel of Toussaint L'Ouverture, from the 1791 slave rising in Saint Domingo through his rule to his betrayal and death in a French fortress.

title: Travels of an Arab Merchant in Soudan (the Black Kingdoms of Central Africa)
short: Travels of an Arab Merchant in Soudan
author: Mohammed ibn Omar el-Tounsy
blurb: Sheikh Mohammed of Tunis recalls years as a young trader in the Black sultanates of Darfur and Wadai: their courts, wars, slave raids and customs. Abridged from the French.

title: St. Domingo, Its Revolution and Its Hero, Toussaint Louverture
author: Charles Wyllys Elliott
blurb: An 1855 New York lecture on the life of Toussaint Louverture: slavery in St. Domingo, the revolution, his rule, his betrayal by Napoleon and death in a French prison.

title: A Colored Man Round the World
short: A Colored Man Round the World
author: David F. Dorr
blurb: David F. Dorr, enslaved in New Orleans, describes his three-year tour of 1851–54 with his owner through England, France, Germany, Italy, Constantinople, Greece, Egypt and the Holy Land.

title: Official Report of the Niger Valley Exploring Party
short: Report of the Niger Valley Exploring Party
author: Martin Robison Delany
blurb: Martin Delany's report of his 1859–60 journey to Liberia and the Yoruba country seeking land for African American settlement, with his treaty at Abbeokuta and his British tour.

title: The Rising Son; or, The Antecedents and Advancement of the Colored Race
author: William Wells Brown
blurb: William Wells Brown's history of the African race: ancient Ethiopia, Egypt and Carthage, Africa and the slave trade, Liberia, Haiti, Jamaica, Black America through the Civil War, and biographies.

title: Froudacity: West Indian Fables by James Anthony Froude, Explained by J. J. Thomas
author: J. J. Thomas
blurb: The Trinidadian schoolmaster J. J. Thomas answers James Anthony Froude's The English in the West Indies point by point, defending Black West Indians and their fitness for self-government.

title: Egyptian Tales, Translated from the Papyri: First Series, IVth to XIIth Dynasty
author: W. M. Flinders Petrie (ed.)
blurb: Four tales from Middle Kingdom papyri: King Khufu and the magicians, the eloquent peasant, the shipwrecked sailor, and the exile Sanehat, translated by Flinders Petrie with his remarks on each.

title: Egyptian Tales, Translated from the Papyri: Second Series, XVIIIth to XIXth Dynasty
author: W. M. Flinders Petrie (ed.)
blurb: Four New Kingdom tales from the papyri: the taking of Joppa, the doomed prince, the two brothers Anpu and Bata, and Setna and the magic book, with Petrie’s remarks.

title: How the Black St. Domingo Legion Saved the Patriot Army in the Siege of Savannah, 1779
short: The Black St. Domingo Legion at Savannah
author: T. G. Steward
blurb: Chaplain T. G. Steward tells how free Black volunteers from Saint-Domingue covered the retreat at Savannah in 1779, among them men who would later lead the Haitian Revolution.

title: Zanzibar Tales, Told by Natives of the East Coast of Africa
author: George W. Bateman (trans.)
blurb: Ten Swahili tales told in Zanzibar, of the monkey and the shark, the clever hare, the gazelle who served Haamdaanee, and the boy hunter, translated by George W. Bateman.

title: Jamaican Song and Story: Annancy Stories, Digging Sings, Ring Tunes, and Dancing Tunes
author: Walter Jekyll (ed.)
blurb: Annancy stories, digging-sings, ring tunes and dancing tunes collected from Black Jamaicans by Walter Jekyll, with his notes on their speech, and essays on their African and English roots.

title: The Black Man, the Father of Civilization, Proven by Biblical History
short: The Black Man, the Father of Civilization
author: James Morris Webb
blurb: An evangelist argues from the Bible that Ham’s descendants founded civilization and Solomon and Jesus were of Black descent; with Pixley ka Isaka Seme’s oration "The Regeneration of Africa".

title: Native Life in South Africa, Before and Since the European War and the Boer Rebellion
author: Sol T. Plaatje
blurb: Sol Plaatje, secretary of the South African Native National Congress, documents the 1913 Natives' Land Act, the evictions it caused, the deputation to London, and the Boer rebellion.

title: Alexander Crummell: An Apostle of Negro Culture
author: William H. Ferris
blurb: William H. Ferris's 1920 tribute to Alexander Crummell, the scholar-priest who studied at Cambridge, worked twenty years in Liberia, and founded the American Negro Academy.

title: Colored Americans in the Wars of 1776 and 1812
author: William C. Nell
blurb: William C. Nell’s state-by-state record of Black soldiers and sailors in the Revolution and the War of 1812, from Crispus Attucks to the free colored battalions at New Orleans.

title: The Black Man: His Antecedents, His Genius, and His Achievements
author: William Wells Brown
blurb: William Wells Brown’s memoir of his life, an essay on the African past, and fifty-seven sketches of Black achievers, from Banneker, Toussaint and Nat Turner to Douglass and Frances Watkins.

title: The Negro in the American Rebellion: His Heroism and His Fidelity
short: The Negro in the American Rebellion
author: William Wells Brown
blurb: William Wells Brown’s record of Black soldiers and sailors from the Revolution and 1812 through slave revolts and the Civil War: Fort Wagner, Port Hudson, Fort Pillow, Olustee, and Petersburg.

title: History of the Negro Race in America from 1619 to 1880, Volume 1
short: History of the Negro Race in America, I
author: George Washington Williams
blurb: Williams's first volume: the unity of mankind, African kingdoms, Sierra Leone and Liberia, slavery in each of the thirteen colonies, Black soldiers in the Revolution, and slavery under the Constitution.

title: History of the Negro Race in America from 1619 to 1880, Volume 2
short: History of the Negro Race in America, II
author: George Washington Williams
blurb: Williams's second volume, 1800 to 1880: the slavery debates, the anti-slavery movement, insurrections, Black soldiers and sailors, the Civil War and emancipation, Reconstruction, and Black churches and leaders after freedom.

title: Black and White: Land, Labor, and Politics in the South
author: T. Thomas Fortune
blurb: Journalist T. Thomas Fortune examines land, labor and politics in the post-Reconstruction South, arguing that its troubles are those of capital and labor, rooted in land monopoly, with Senate testimony.

title: The Black Phalanx: A History of the Negro Soldiers of the United States in the Wars of 1775-1812, 1861-65
author: Joseph T. Wilson
blurb: A veteran of the 54th Massachusetts records the service of Black soldiers in the Revolution, the War of 1812 and the Civil War: recruiting, campaigns, Fort Pillow, rosters and schools.

title: The Suppression of the African Slave-Trade to the United States of America, 1638-1870
short: The Suppression of the African Slave-Trade
author: W. E. B. Du Bois
blurb: Du Bois's Harvard dissertation traces colonial, state, national and international efforts to suppress the African slave trade to the United States, 1638 to 1870, with chronological appendices of legislation.

title: Frederick Douglass: A Biography
author: Charles W. Chesnutt
blurb: A short life of Frederick Douglass by the novelist Charles W. Chesnutt: slavery in Maryland, escape, the anti-slavery platform, his newspaper, and public office after the war.

title: The Negro
author: W. E. B. Du Bois
blurb: Du Bois's short history of African peoples: Ethiopia and Egypt, the kingdoms of the Niger, Guinea, Congo and southern Africa, African culture, the slave trade, and the Americas.

title: The Education of the Negro Prior to 1861
short: The Education of the Negro Prior to 1861
author: Carter G. Woodson
blurb: Woodson's history of how enslaved and free Black Americans gained schooling before 1861, through missionaries, Quakers, private schools and self-teaching, and of the laws that forbade it, with documents.

title: The Journal of Negro History, Volume 1, 1916
author: Carter G. Woodson (ed.)
blurb: The first volume of The Journal of Negro History, edited by Carter G. Woodson: the articles, historical documents, book reviews and notes of its four 1916 issues.

title: The Negro in Literature and Art in the United States
short: The Negro in Literature and Art
author: Benjamin Brawley
blurb: Benjamin Brawley surveys Black American achievement in literature, oratory, the stage, painting, sculpture and music, from Phillis Wheatley and Dunbar to Tanner and Gilpin, with a study of bibliography.

title: A Century of Negro Migration
author: Carter G. Woodson
blurb: Carter G. Woodson traces Black migration north and west from about 1815 to the First World War: refuge in free states, colonization schemes, the 1879 Exodus, and the wartime exodus.

title: Two Colored Women with the American Expeditionary Forces
short: Two Colored Women with the A. E. F.
author: Addie W. Hunton and Kathryn M. Johnson
blurb: Two YMCA workers tell of fifteen months with Black American troops in France, 1918–1919: labor battalions, combat divisions, canteens, schooling, leave areas and the reburial of the dead.

title: A Social History of the American Negro
short: A Social History of the American Negro
author: Benjamin Brawley
blurb: Brawley's history of the Negro problem in the United States from the slave trade to 1920: insurrections, abolition, Liberia, the Civil War, Reconstruction, disfranchisement, lynching and the Great Migration.

title: The History of the Negro Church
short: The History of the Negro Church
author: Carter G. Woodson
blurb: Woodson's history of the Black church in America, from colonial missionaries and pioneer preachers through the independent church movement, the Civil War and Reconstruction, to the churches of 1921.

title: The Gift of Black Folk: The Negroes in the Making of America
author: W. E. B. Du Bois
blurb: Du Bois surveys what Black Americans gave the nation: exploration, labor, soldiering in every war, the struggle that widened democracy, Reconstruction, women’s freedom, folk song, art and literature, and spirit.

title: Clotel; or, The President's Daughter
author: William Wells Brown
blurb: Currer, once Thomas Jefferson's housekeeper, and their daughters Clotel and Althesa are sold at auction in Richmond; Brown's novel follows the three women through slavery in the South.

title: Our Nig; or, Sketches from the Life of a Free Black
author: Harriet E. Wilson
blurb: Frado, a mixed-race girl left by her white mother, is bound as a servant to a white Northern family, the Bellmonts, and endures years of cruelty from her mistress.

title: Iola Leroy; or, Shadows Uplifted
author: Frances E. W. Harper
blurb: Iola Leroy, raised as white by her Mississippi planter father, is sold into slavery after his death; freed by Union troops, she nurses the wounded and seeks her scattered family.

title: The Uncalled
author: Paul Laurence Dunbar
blurb: Freddie Brent, orphaned in a small Ohio town and raised by the stern Miss Hester Prime, is pressed toward the ministry he does not feel called to.

title: The Conjure Woman
author: Charles W. Chesnutt
blurb: A Northern grape grower settles in North Carolina, where Uncle Julius, once enslaved there, tells tales of conjure and slavery; three uncollected Julius stories and an essay are appended.

title: The Wife of His Youth and Other Stories of the Color Line, and Selected Essays
author: Charles W. Chesnutt
blurb: Nine stories of the color line, from Blue Vein society in a Northern city to a North Carolina jail, followed by three essays on race and the vote.

title: Imperium in Imperio
author: Sutton E. Griggs
blurb: Berl Trout's papers tell of Belton Piedmont and Bernard Belgrave, two educated Black men whose lives lead them into a secret national government of Black Americans, the Imperium.

title: The House Behind the Cedars
author: Charles W. Chesnutt
blurb: John Warwick, who has passed as white in South Carolina, returns to his mother's house in Patesville, North Carolina, to take his sister Rena into the white world.

title: The Marrow of Tradition
author: Charles W. Chesnutt
blurb: In Wellington, North Carolina, newspaper editor Major Carteret and his allies plot white rule, while the Black doctor William Miller and his wife Janet face mounting racial violence.

title: The Sport of the Gods
author: Paul Laurence Dunbar
blurb: When Berry Hamilton, a trusted Black servant in a Southern town, is falsely convicted of theft, his wife and children move to New York, where city life changes them.

title: Unfettered: A Novel
author: Sutton E. Griggs
blurb: Freed from a forced engagement, Morlene will marry Dorlan Warthell only if he can show how his race may be freed; the novel is followed by his answer, "Dorlan’s Plan".

title: Of One Blood; or, The Hidden Self
author: Pauline E. Hopkins
blurb: Reuel Briggs, a Harvard medical student who hides his Black ancestry, studies mesmerism and the occult, then joins an archaeological expedition to the ruins of ancient Meroë in Ethiopia.

title: Winona: A Tale of Negro Life in the South and Southwest
author: Pauline E. Hopkins
blurb: Winona, daughter of a white chief of the Seneca and a fugitive slave, is carried into slavery in Missouri with her foster brother Judah, who escapes to join John Brown.

title: Light Ahead for the Negro
author: Edward A. Johnson
blurb: A white Northerner bound south in 1906 is carried off in a runaway airship and wakes a century later in Georgia, where education and goodwill have solved the race problem.

title: The Colonel's Dream
author: Charles W. Chesnutt
blurb: Colonel Henry French, a retired New York merchant, returns to his Southern hometown of Clarendon and tries to revive it with a cotton mill and justice for its Black citizens.

title: The Hindered Hand; or, The Reign of the Repressionist
author: Sutton E. Griggs
blurb: Black families in Almaville, a Southern city, contend with racial passing, lynching and political repression; a closing essay answers the anti-Negro crusade of Thomas Dixon, Jr.

title: The Quest of the Silver Fleece
short: The Quest of the Silver Fleece
author: W. E. B. Du Bois
blurb: Bles Alwyn, a student at a Black school in Alabama, and Zora, a girl of the swamp, plant a cotton crop; the story runs from the cotton belt to Washington.

title: The Autobiography of an Ex-Colored Man
short: The Autobiography of an Ex-Colored Man
author: James Weldon Johnson
blurb: The anonymous narrator, light-skinned and born in Georgia, recalls a Connecticut boyhood, years as a ragtime pianist in New York and Europe, and his decision to pass as white.

title: The Conquest: The Story of a Negro Pioneer
author: Oscar Micheaux
blurb: Oscar Micheaux’s autobiographical novel of a young Black man who leaves Illinois to homestead alone on the Rosebud lands of South Dakota, amid booms, drought and a divided love.

title: The Fire in the Flint
author: Walter F. White
blurb: Kenneth Harper, a Black doctor trained in the North, returns to his Georgia hometown meaning to avoid the race question, until sharecroppers’ organizing and the Klan draw him in.

title: Fire!! A Quarterly Devoted to the Younger Negro Artists, Volume One, Number One, November 1926
author: Wallace Thurman, Langston Hughes, Zora Neale Hurston, et al.
blurb: The only issue of the Harlem Renaissance magazine Fire!!: stories by Thurman, Hurston, Bennett and Bruce Nugent, Hurston’s play Color Struck, poems by Cullen, Hughes, Bontemps and others, and essays.

title: Poems on Various Subjects, Religious and Moral
author: Phillis Wheatley
blurb: Elegies, hymns, odes and verse letters by Phillis Wheatley, brought from Africa as a child and enslaved in Boston, with the attestation of her authorship signed by eighteen Boston notables.

title: Sketches of Southern Life
author: Frances E. W. Harper
blurb: Frances Harper’s poems in the voice of Aunt Chloe, a freedwoman recalling slavery, emancipation, learning to read and Reconstruction politics, with temperance and religious poems and a prose allegory.

title: The Complete Poems of Paul Laurence Dunbar
short: The Complete Poems of Paul Laurence Dunbar
author: Paul Laurence Dunbar
blurb: Dunbar's four collections, Lyrics of Lowly Life, of the Hearthside, of Love and Laughter, and of Sunshine and Shadow, in literary English and in dialect, with Howells's introduction.

title: Fifty Years and Other Poems
author: James Weldon Johnson
blurb: James Weldon Johnson’s first book of poems: "Fifty Years", for the semi-centennial of emancipation, "O Black and Unknown Bards", lyrics and sonnets, and the dialect "Jingles & Croons".

title: The Book of American Negro Poetry
short: The Book of American Negro Poetry
author: James Weldon Johnson (ed.)
blurb: James Weldon Johnson's anthology of thirty-one poets, from Dunbar and Braithwaite to Claude McKay and Anne Spencer, opening with his long essay on the Negro's creative genius.

title: Harlem Shadows: The Poems of Claude McKay
author: Claude McKay
blurb: Claude McKay’s poems of Harlem and of Jamaica remembered: love lyrics, nature poems, and the sonnets of protest of 1919, among them "If We Must Die", "The Lynching" and "America".

title: Negro Folk Rhymes, Wise and Otherwise
author: Thomas W. Talley
blurb: More than three hundred secular folk rhymes of Black Southerners, dance, play, love, courtship, nursery and wise-saying rhymes among them, followed by Talley's study of their origins.

title: An Appeal in Favor of That Class of Americans Called Africans
author: Lydia Maria Child
blurb: Lydia Maria Child's case against slavery: its history and economics, slavery in other ages, its hold on American politics, colonization, the intellect and character of Africans, and Northern prejudice.

title: Uncle Tom's Cabin; or, Life Among the Lowly
author: Harriet Beecher Stowe
blurb: Stowe's antislavery novel follows Uncle Tom, sold away from his Kentucky home and carried down the Mississippi, and Eliza Harris, who escapes across the icy Ohio with her son.

title: Journal of a Residence on a Georgian Plantation in 1838-1839
author: Frances Anne Kemble
blurb: Letters the English actress wrote in 1838-39 from her husband's rice and cotton plantations on the Georgia coast, describing the work, sickness and suffering of the people enslaved there.

title: Army Life in a Black Regiment
short: Army Life in a Black Regiment
author: Thomas Wentworth Higginson
blurb: Higginson recounts commanding the First South Carolina Volunteers, a regiment of former slaves, in 1862-64: camp life, raids up Southern rivers, and the spirituals his soldiers sang.

title: The Upanishads
author: Anonymous
blurb: The Isa, Katha and Kena Upanishads, the Vedic dialogues on the Self and Brahman, including Nachiketas’s questions to Death, translated with a commentary by Swami Paramananda.

title: The Tao Teh King, or the Tao and Its Characteristics
author: Lao-Tse
blurb: The eighty-one short chapters of the Taoist classic on the nameless Tao, the virtue of yielding and non-action, and the sage ruler, in Legge’s translation with rhymed passages.

title: The Dhammapada: A Collection of Verses, Being One of the Canonical Books of the Buddhists
author: Anonymous
blurb: The 423 verses of the Dhammapada, the Buddhist canon’s best-loved book of sayings on the mind, self-conquest, the path and the arhat, in twenty-six chapters, translated from Pali.

title: The Song Celestial; or, Bhagavad-Gîtâ (from the Mahâbhârata)
author: Anonymous
blurb: On the eve of battle Prince Arjuna loses heart, and Krishna, his charioteer, teaches him of duty, the deathless soul, devotion and the ways of yoga, in Arnold’s blank verse.

title: Rubáiyát of Omar Khayyám
author: Omar Khayyám
blurb: FitzGerald’s English quatrains after the Persian astronomer-poet, on wine, the passing of time and the riddle of fate, in the first and fifth editions, with his introduction and notes.

title: The Gulistan
author: Sa'di
blurb: Sa’di’s thirteenth-century “Rose Garden”: short tales, maxims and verses on kings, dervishes, contentment, silence, love, old age, education and the conduct of life.

title: The Persian Mystics: Jalálu'd-dín Rúmí
author: Jalálu'd-dín Rúmí
blurb: F. Hadland Davis introduces Sufism and the life of the thirteenth-century poet Rúmí, then gives selections from his lyrics to Shams of Tabriz and from the Masnavi.

title: The Imitation of Christ
author: Thomas à Kempis
blurb: The fifteenth-century devotional classic in four books: counsels for the spiritual life, the inner life, dialogues between Christ and the disciple on inward consolation, and the sacrament.

title: The Apocrypha: The Deuterocanonical Books of the Bible, King James Version
author: King James Version
blurb: The books printed between the Testaments in the King James Bible, among them Tobit, Judith, the Wisdom of Solomon, Ecclesiasticus, Baruch and the Maccabees.

title: The Holy Bible, Containing the Old and New Testaments: The King James Version
author: King James Version
blurb: The Old and New Testaments in the Authorized Version of 1611, from Genesis to Revelation, with verse numbers as printed; the longer books are divided into reading-sized parts.

title: The Pilgrim's Progress from This World to That Which Is to Come
author: John Bunyan
blurb: Part One of Bunyan’s allegory, told as a dream: Christian’s journey from the City of Destruction through the Slough of Despond, Vanity Fair and Doubting Castle to the Celestial City.

title: The Practice of the Presence of God, the Best Rule of a Holy Life
short: The Practice of the Presence of God
author: Brother Lawrence
blurb: Conversations with and letters of Brother Lawrence, a seventeenth-century Carmelite lay brother and cook in Paris, on living in continual awareness of God amid ordinary work.

title: Religious Experience and Journal of Mrs. Jarena Lee, Giving an Account of Her Call to Preach the Gospel
short: Religious Experience of Mrs. Jarena Lee
author: Jarena Lee
blurb: Jarena Lee, the first woman Richard Allen allowed to preach in the African Methodist Episcopal Church, tells of her conversion, her call to preach, and years of travelling ministry.

title: The Koran (Al-Qur'an)
author: J. M. Rodwell (trans.)
blurb: J. M. Rodwell’s English Koran of 1861, its suras arranged in the order he believed they were revealed, with his notes and preface and an introduction by G. Margoliouth.

title: Biography of a Slave; Being the Experiences of Rev. Charles Thompson, a Preacher of the United Brethren Church, While a Slave in the South
author: Charles Thompson
blurb: Charles Thompson, later a United Brethren preacher, recalls slavery in Mississippi and Tennessee: being sold from his mother, learning to write, preaching on the plantation, and running away.

title: The Light of Asia
author: Edwin Arnold
blurb: Edwin Arnold’s blank-verse life of Prince Siddartha: his sheltered youth, the sights of age, sickness and death, his renunciation, enlightenment, and the Law he taught.

title: The Speeches & Table-Talk of the Prophet Mohammad
short: The Speeches & Table-Talk of the Prophet
author: The Prophet Muhammad
blurb: Passages of the Koran arranged as the Prophet Muhammad’s speeches at Mecca and Medina, with the law he gave and his recorded sayings, introduced by Stanley Lane-Poole.

title: Egyptian Ideas of the Future Life
short: Egyptian Ideas of the Future Life
author: E. A. Wallis Budge
blurb: Budge surveys what the ancient Egyptians believed about God, Osiris, the resurrection, the judgment of the dead, and the parts of the soul, quoting the religious texts throughout.

title: Egyptian Literature, Comprising Egyptian Tales, Hymns, Litanies, Invocations, the Book of the Dead, and Cuneiform Writings
author: Epiphanius Wilson (ed.)
blurb: Ancient Egyptian writing in English translation: the Book of the Dead, hymns and litanies, tales such as the Shipwrecked Sailor, the Tell Amarna letters and the poem of Penta-Our.

title: Life of Charles T. Walker, D.D. ("The Black Spurgeon"), Pastor Mt. Olivet Baptist Church, New York City
author: Silas Xavier Floyd
blurb: The life of the Georgia-born Baptist preacher called "the Black Spurgeon": his pastorates in Augusta and New York, his journey to the Holy Land, sermons, addresses and anecdotes.

title: As a Man Thinketh
author: James Allen
blurb: James Allen’s short essay of 1903 on the power of thought over character, circumstance, health and achievement, and on calm self-control as the fruit of right thinking.

title: The Defects of the Negro Church
short: The Defects of the Negro Church
author: Orishatukeh Faduma
blurb: An American Negro Academy paper by the Sierra Leonean minister Orishatukeh Faduma on the Negro church’s failings: outward show, rural neglect, an untrained ministry and excessive emotionalism.

title: The Egyptian Book of the Dead: Translation and Commentary
short: The Egyptian Book of the Dead
author: P. Le Page Renouf and Édouard Naville (trans.)
blurb: The Egyptian funerary texts known as the Book of the Dead, chapter by chapter, in the translation begun by Peter Le Page Renouf and completed by Édouard Naville, with commentary.

title: John Jasper, the Unmatched Negro Philosopher and Preacher
author: William E. Hatcher
blurb: A Richmond Baptist minister’s portrait of John Jasper, the preacher born in slavery who founded Sixth Mount Zion Church, with his sermons, among them the famous "The Sun Do Move."

title: The Kybalion: A Study of the Hermetic Philosophy of Ancient Egypt and Greece
author: Three Initiates
blurb: An anonymous 1908 primer of “Hermetic” philosophy that sets out seven principles, from Mentalism to Gender, and applies them to mental transmutation and the mastery of mood and circumstance.

title: Religious Folk-Songs of the Southern Negroes
short: Religious Folk-Songs of the Southern Negroes
author: Howard W. Odum
blurb: A 1909 study of the spirituals sung by Black Southerners, quoting hundreds of verses on sin, Satan, heaven and judgment and comparing them with earlier published collections.

title: Legends of the Gods: The Egyptian Texts, Edited with Translations
author: E. A. Wallis Budge
blurb: English translations of Egyptian myths from temple and papyrus texts: the creation, Ra and Isis, the destruction of mankind, the Osiris legend, Horus, and other legends of the gods.

title: Gitanjali (Song Offerings)
author: Rabindranath Tagore
blurb: One hundred and three song offerings to God, translated by Tagore from his Bengali poems into English prose, with W. B. Yeats’s introduction to the 1912 edition.

title: Pirke Avot: The Sayings of the Jewish Fathers
short: The Sayings of the Jewish Fathers
author: Joseph I. Gorfinkle (trans.)
blurb: The Mishnah’s tractate of ethical sayings of the rabbis, from Moses receiving the Torah at Sinai onward, translated with an introduction and notes for a Jewish classics series.

title: Gideon Bands, for Work within the Race and for Work without the Race: A Message to the Colored People of the United States
author: Francis J. Grimké
blurb: A 1913 sermon at Washington’s Fifteenth Street Presbyterian Church calling on Black Americans to form bands of committed workers for the race, as Gideon chose his three hundred.

title: The Book of the Dead
author: E. A. Wallis Budge
blurb: A short introduction by the British Museum’s Egyptologist to the Book of the Dead: its title, Thoth and Osiris, the judgment of the dead, and the contents of its chapters.

title: The Holy Piby: The Black Man's Bible
author: Robert Athlyi Rogers
blurb: The scripture of Shepherd Athlyi’s Afro Athlican Constructive Church: four books of creation, law and apostles that name Marcus Garvey an apostle and promise the redemption of Ethiopia’s children.

title: The Golden Asse
author: Apuleius
blurb: Adlington's 1566 translation of the Latin novel by Apuleius of Madaura in North Africa, in which Lucius, turned into an ass by magic, passes from master to master.

title: Candide
author: Voltaire
blurb: Voltaire's satire of young Candide, taught by Pangloss that all is for the best in the best of possible worlds, then thrown into a world of war and cruelty.

title: Pride and Prejudice
author: Jane Austen
blurb: Mrs. Bennet means to see her five daughters married; the second, Elizabeth, takes a quick dislike to proud Mr. Darcy, wealthy friend of their new neighbour Mr. Bingley.

title: Frankenstein; or, The Modern Prometheus
author: Mary Wollstonecraft Shelley
blurb: In letters to his sister, the Arctic explorer Robert Walton records the story of Victor Frankenstein, a young Genevan scientist who gives life to a creature he then abandons.

title: The Prose Tales of Alexander Pushkin
short: The Prose Tales of Alexander Pushkin
author: Alexander Pushkin
blurb: Keane's translation of Pushkin's tales, among them The Captain's Daughter, The Queen of Spades, Doubrovsky and the unfinished Peter the Great's Negro, about the poet's African great-grandfather.

title: The Count of Monte Cristo
author: Alexandre Dumas
blurb: Edmond Dantès, a young Marseilles sailor, is falsely denounced at his betrothal feast and imprisoned in the Château d'If, where a fellow prisoner tells him of hidden treasure.

title: The Three Musketeers
author: Alexandre Dumas
blurb: In 1625 young d’Artagnan comes from Gascony to Paris and, with the musketeers Athos, Porthos and Aramis, is drawn into the intrigues between the queen and Cardinal Richelieu.

title: Jane Eyre: An Autobiography
author: Charlotte Brontë
blurb: Jane Eyre tells of her orphaned childhood with her Reed relations and at Lowood school, and of her life as governess at Thornfield Hall, the home of Mr. Rochester.

title: Wuthering Heights
author: Emily Brontë
blurb: Lockwood, a tenant at Thrushcross Grange, hears from the housekeeper Nelly Dean the history of his landlord Heathcliff and the Earnshaw and Linton families of the Yorkshire moors.

title: Camille (La Dame aux Camélias)
author: Alexandre Dumas fils
blurb: Dumas fils's novel of Marguerite Gautier, a Paris courtesan who gives up her life of pleasure for love of young Armand Duval; Verdi drew La Traviata from it.

title: Moby-Dick; or, The Whale
author: Herman Melville
blurb: Ishmael ships aboard the Nantucket whaler Pequod, whose captain, Ahab, means to hunt down the white whale that took his leg; chapters on whales and whaling run alongside the voyage.

title: The Piazza Tales
author: Herman Melville
blurb: Melville's 1856 collection: The Piazza, Bartleby, the Encantadas sketches of the Galápagos, The Bell-Tower, and Benito Cereno, in which an American captain boards a Spanish slave ship off Chile.

title: Madame Bovary
author: Gustave Flaubert
blurb: Eleanor Marx-Aveling's translation of Flaubert's novel of Emma, wife of a dull country doctor in Normandy, who seeks the passion of the romances she read as a girl.

title: A Tale of Two Cities
author: Charles Dickens
blurb: Freed after eighteen years in the Bastille, Doctor Manette goes to London with his daughter Lucie; years later the French Revolution draws their family back to Paris.

title: Great Expectations
author: Charles Dickens
blurb: Pip, an orphan raised by his sister and her husband, the blacksmith Joe Gargery, on the marshes, learns that an unknown benefactor means to make him a gentleman.

title: Les Misérables
author: Victor Hugo
blurb: Jean Valjean, freed after nineteen years in the galleys, rebuilds his life and raises the orphan Cosette while Inspector Javert hunts him, up to the Paris insurrection of 1832.

title: Notes from the Underground
author: Fyodor Dostoevsky
blurb: A retired official in his St. Petersburg corner rails against reason and progress, then recalls the humiliations of his youth: an officer, a disastrous dinner, and the prostitute Liza.

title: Crime and Punishment
author: Fyodor Dostoevsky
blurb: In St. Petersburg the impoverished former student Raskolnikov murders an old pawnbroker to test his theory of the extraordinary man, then wrestles with fever, guilt and the examining magistrate Porfiry.

title: The Idiot
author: Fyodor Dostoevsky
blurb: Prince Muishkin, gentle and epileptic, returns to Petersburg after years in a Swiss sanatorium and is drawn into the passions of Nastasia Philipovna, Aglaya Epanchin and the merchant's son Rogojin.

title: War and Peace
author: Leo Tolstoy
blurb: Tolstoy follows the Rostóv and Bolkónski families and Pierre Bezúkhov through the wars with Napoleon from 1805, the invasion of 1812 and the burning of Moscow, with essays on history.

title: Middlemarch: A Study of Provincial Life
author: George Eliot
blurb: Set in a Midlands town around 1830, the novel follows idealistic Dorothea Brooke, the ambitious doctor Tertius Lydgate and their neighbours through marriage, money, religion and political reform.

title: Anna Karenina
author: Leo Tolstoy
blurb: Anna Karenina, wife of a high Petersburg official, falls in love with the officer Vronsky, while the landowner Levin courts Kitty Shtcherbatsky and searches for a meaning to his life.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
author: Fyodor Dostoevsky
blurb: The dissolute landowner Fyodor Karamazov and his sons, the passionate Dmitri, the sceptical Ivan and Alyosha, a novice at the monastery, quarrel over money, a woman and faith in God.

title: Adventures of Huckleberry Finn
author: Mark Twain
blurb: Huck Finn tells how he fled his drunken father and floated down the Mississippi on a raft with Jim, who was escaping slavery, through feuds, frauds and river towns.

title: The Kreutzer Sonata and Other Stories
short: The Kreutzer Sonata and Other Stories
author: Leo Tolstoy
blurb: Tolstoy's novella of a man telling a fellow traveller how jealousy drove him to kill his wife, with Tolstoy's afterword and four tales, including Ivan the Fool.

title: The Picture of Dorian Gray
author: Oscar Wilde
blurb: Under the influence of Lord Henry Wotton, the young Dorian Gray wishes that the portrait Basil Hallward has painted of him might grow old in his place.

title: The Tragedy of Pudd'nhead Wilson
author: Mark Twain
blurb: In Dawson's Landing, Missouri, the enslaved Roxy, who is one-sixteenth Black, swaps her baby son with her master's infant, and the town's derided lawyer, Pudd'nhead Wilson, collects fingerprints.

title: Heart of Darkness
author: Joseph Conrad
blurb: Marlow tells of his voyage up the Congo River for a Belgian trading company to find the ivory agent Kurtz; in 1975 Chinua Achebe called the novella racist.

title: Ulysses
author: James Joyce
blurb: Over one day in Dublin, 16 June 1904, Joyce follows the advertising canvasser Leopold Bloom, the teacher Stephen Dedalus and Bloom's wife Molly through eighteen episodes in shifting styles.

title: The Iliad
author: Homer
blurb: Samuel Butler's prose translation of Homer's epic of the Trojan War, from the quarrel between Agamemnon and Achilles through the fighting on the plain before Troy.

title: The Odyssey
author: Homer
blurb: Samuel Butler's prose translation of Homer's epic of Ulysses' long voyage home from Troy and of the suitors besieging his wife Penelope in Ithaca, with Butler's prefaces and notes.

title: Oedipus the King, Oedipus at Colonus, Antigone
author: Sophocles
blurb: F. Storr's verse translation of Sophocles's three Theban plays: Oedipus the King, Oedipus at Colonus, where the blind exile finds his resting place near Athens, and Antigone.

title: The Comedies of Terence
author: Terence
blurb: George Colman's 1765 blank-verse translation of the six comedies of Terence, the African-born Roman playwright: The Andrian, The Eunuch, The Self-Tormentor, The Brothers, The Step-Mother and Phormio.

title: The Aeneid
author: Virgil
blurb: John Dryden's 1697 verse translation of Virgil's epic of the Trojan prince Aeneas, who escapes burning Troy, loves and leaves Dido of Carthage, and wins a new home in Italy.

title: The Divine Comedy
author: Dante Alighieri
blurb: Longfellow's line-for-line translation of Dante's journey through Hell, Purgatory and Paradise, guided by Virgil and then by Beatrice, followed by Longfellow's six sonnets on the poem.

title: The Tragedy of Romeo and Juliet
author: William Shakespeare
blurb: Shakespeare's tragedy of two young lovers of Verona, children of the feuding houses of Montague and Capulet, who marry in secret.

title: Hamlet, Prince of Denmark
author: William Shakespeare
blurb: Shakespeare's tragedy of the Prince of Denmark, who learns from his father's ghost that his uncle, now king and married to his mother, murdered his father.

title: The History of Don Quixote of La Mancha
author: Miguel de Cervantes
blurb: Ormsby's translation of both parts of Cervantes's novel, in which a Manchegan gentleman crazed by books of chivalry rides out as a knight-errant with his squire, Sancho Panza.

title: The Tragedy of King Lear
author: William Shakespeare
blurb: Shakespeare's tragedy of an old king of Britain who divides his kingdom between the two daughters who flatter him and banishes the youngest, who will not.

title: Othello, the Moor of Venice
author: William Shakespeare
blurb: Shakespeare's tragedy of a Moorish general in the service of Venice whose ensign, Iago, works on him until he suspects his wife, Desdemona, of loving Cassio.

title: The Tragedy of Julius Caesar
author: William Shakespeare
blurb: Shakespeare's tragedy of the conspiracy of Brutus and Cassius against Julius Caesar, his murder in the Capitol, Mark Antony's funeral speech, and the civil war that follows.

title: Macbeth
author: William Shakespeare
blurb: Shakespeare's tragedy of a Scottish general who, told by three witches that he will be king, is urged on by his wife to murder King Duncan.

title: The Tempest
author: William Shakespeare
blurb: Shakespeare's late play of Prospero, the exiled Duke of Milan, who with his daughter Miranda and the spirit Ariel wrecks his old enemies on his island.

title: Faust: A Tragedy
author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe
blurb: Bayard Taylor's translation, in the original metres, of the first part of Goethe's tragedy, in which the scholar Faust makes a pact with Mephistopheles and loves Margaret.

title: Leaves of Grass
author: Walt Whitman
blurb: The final, 1891–92 edition of Whitman's poems, arranged in his own clusters: Song of Myself, Children of Adam, Calamus, Drum-Taps, the Lincoln elegies and the late annexes.

title: The Art of War
author: Sun Tzu
blurb: The ancient Chinese treatise on strategy in thirteen chapters, on planning, deception, terrain and spies, in Lionel Giles’s 1910 translation with his introduction and commentary.

title: The Analects of Confucius
author: Confucius
blurb: The sayings and conversations of Confucius and his disciples, in twenty books, on learning, filial piety, ritual, government and the superior man, in James Legge’s translation.

title: Apology, Crito and Phædo of Socrates
author: Plato
blurb: Cary's translation of Plato's dialogues on the trial and death of Socrates: his defence to the jury, his refusal to escape from prison, and his last talk, on the soul.

title: The Republic
author: Plato
blurb: Socrates and his companions ask what justice is and build an ideal city ruled by philosopher-kings, in Jowett’s translation with his long Introduction and Analysis.

title: The Ethics of Aristotle
author: Aristotle
blurb: D. P. Chase's translation of the Nicomachean Ethics, Aristotle's inquiry into happiness as the chief good, the moral and intellectual virtues, justice, friendship and pleasure, with J. A. Smith's introduction.

title: A Selection from the Discourses of Epictetus, with the Encheiridion
author: Epictetus
blurb: The Stoic teacher’s discourses on what is and is not in our power, freedom, providence and tranquillity, as recorded by Arrian, with the Encheiridion, his short manual of conduct.

title: Meditations
author: Marcus Aurelius
blurb: The Roman emperor’s private notebooks of Stoic reflection on duty, death, nature and self-command, in Casaubon’s 1634 translation, with letters between Marcus and his tutor Fronto.

title: The Confessions of Saint Augustine
author: Saint Augustine
blurb: Pusey's translation of the thirteen books in which Augustine of Hippo, born in North Africa, tells God of his youth, his years as a Manichee and his conversion in Milan.

title: The Consolation of Philosophy
author: Boethius
blurb: Imprisoned and awaiting execution in 524, the Roman statesman Boethius is visited by Philosophy, who in prose and song consoles him on fortune, happiness, evil, providence and free will.

title: The Prince
author: Niccolò Machiavelli
blurb: Machiavelli's handbook for a new prince on gaining and holding a state, drawn from Florentine politics and ancient history, with his life of Castruccio Castracani.

title: Essays of Michel de Montaigne
author: Michel de Montaigne
blurb: Montaigne’s three books of essays on friendship, education, cannibals, cruelty, experience, death and himself, in Cotton’s translation as edited by Hazlitt, with a life and letters.

title: The Thoughts of Blaise Pascal
author: Blaise Pascal
blurb: The fragments of Pascal’s unfinished defence of Christianity, on the misery and greatness of man, diversion, the wager, prophecy and miracles, with his Memorial of 1654.

title: Common Sense
author: Thomas Paine
blurb: Paine's 1776 pamphlet urging the American colonies to declare independence from Britain, attacking monarchy and hereditary succession, with his appendix and address to the Quakers.

title: An Inquiry into the Nature and Causes of the Wealth of Nations
author: Adam Smith
blurb: Adam Smith’s 1776 inquiry into the division of labour, money, prices, wages, profit and rent, capital, the mercantile system, colonies, and the revenue and expenses of the state.

title: A Vindication of the Rights of Woman
short: A Vindication of the Rights of Woman
author: Mary Wollstonecraft
blurb: Wollstonecraft argues that women are rational beings denied education and independence, criticises Rousseau and other writers on female character, and proposes national education for both sexes.

title: Manifesto of the Communist Party
author: Karl Marx and Friedrich Engels
blurb: The 1848 pamphlet of the Communist League sets out a history of class struggle, the rise of the bourgeoisie and proletariat, and the aims of the Communists.

title: Walden, and On the Duty of Civil Disobedience
author: Henry David Thoreau
blurb: Thoreau’s account of two years living alone in a cabin he built by Walden Pond, on economy, reading, solitude, nature and the seasons, with his essay on civil disobedience.

title: On Liberty
author: John Stuart Mill
blurb: Mill's essay on the limits of the power society may rightly exercise over the individual: liberty of thought and discussion, individuality, and the harm principle, with W. L. Courtney's introduction.

title: The Subjection of Women
author: John Stuart Mill
blurb: Mill's 1869 essay arguing that the legal subordination of women to men is wrong in itself and a hindrance to human improvement, and should give way to perfect equality.

title: Thus Spake Zarathustra: A Book for All and None
author: Friedrich Nietzsche
blurb: In prophetic discourses and songs the sage Zarathustra comes down from his mountain to teach the Superman, the will to power and eternal recurrence, with notes by Anthony Ludovici.

title: Beyond Good and Evil
author: Friedrich Nietzsche
blurb: Nietzsche’s 1886 book of numbered aphorisms attacks the prejudices of philosophers and conventional morality and asks what nobility is, closing with the poem “From the Heights.”

title: The Varieties of Religious Experience: A Study in Human Nature
author: William James
blurb: William James’s Gifford Lectures study religion as personal experience: healthy-mindedness and the sick soul, conversion, saintliness and mysticism, drawn from first-hand testimonies.

title: The Natural History of Selborne
author: Gilbert White
blurb: A country parson's letters to two naturalists, 1767-1787, on the birds, beasts, insects, plants and weather of his Hampshire parish, with a few of his poems.

title: The Voyage of the Beagle
author: Charles Darwin
blurb: Darwin’s journal of the Beagle’s 1831–36 voyage: the geology, animals, plants and peoples of South America, the Galapagos, Tahiti, New Zealand, Australia and the coral islands.

title: On the Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selection
author: Charles Darwin
blurb: The first edition of Darwin’s argument that species descend with modification through natural selection, drawing on domestic breeding, instinct, hybridism, the fossil record and geographical distribution.

title: The Chemical History of a Candle: A Course of Lectures Delivered before a Juvenile Audience at the Royal Institution
short: The Chemical History of a Candle
author: Michael Faraday
blurb: Michael Faraday's six Christmas lectures for young people at the Royal Institution, explaining combustion, water, hydrogen, oxygen, air and carbon through a burning candle, with his lecture on platinum.

title: The Descent of Man, and Selection in Relation to Sex
author: Charles Darwin
blurb: Darwin applies evolution to humankind, tracing man’s descent from earlier forms and the growth of mental and moral faculties, and sets out sexual selection across the animal kingdom.

title: The Formation of Vegetable Mould through the Action of Worms, with Observations on Their Habits
author: Charles Darwin
blurb: Darwin's last book: years of experiments and measurements on earthworms, their senses and habits, the soil they bring up, and how they bury stones and ancient buildings.

title: The Autobiography of Charles Darwin
author: Charles Darwin
blurb: Written for his children in 1876, with an 1881 postscript: Darwin recalls school, Edinburgh and Cambridge, the Beagle voyage, marriage, life at Down, and how his books were written.

title: The Colored Inventor: A Record of Fifty Years
author: Henry E. Baker
blurb: A Patent Office examiner reviews fifty years of invention by Black Americans, from Benjamin Banneker to Elijah McCoy, Granville Woods and Jan Matzeliger, and the women inventors among them.

title: The Complete Angler; or, The Contemplative Man's Recreation
author: Izaak Walton
blurb: Walton's 1653 first edition: Piscator the angler walks the Lea with Viator, praising the "contemplative man's recreation" and teaching how to catch trout, chub, carp, pike and more, with songs.

title: Autobiography of Benjamin Franklin
author: Benjamin Franklin
blurb: Benjamin Franklin's own account of his life, from his Boston boyhood and printer's apprenticeship to his scheme of thirteen virtues, public projects and science, with The Way to Wealth.

title: The Physiology of Taste; or, Transcendental Gastronomy
author: Jean Anthelme Brillat-Savarin
blurb: Brillat-Savarin's meditations on the senses, appetite, food, thirst, frying, coffee and chocolate, the pleasures of the table, sleep, obesity and fasting, with anecdotes and recipes.

title: Notes on Nursing: What It Is, and What It Is Not
author: Florence Nightingale
blurb: Florence Nightingale's plain advice to every woman who has charge of the sick: fresh air, warmth, light, quiet, cleanliness, food, bedding and the close observation of the patient.

title: Self-Help; with Illustrations of Conduct and Perseverance
author: Samuel Smiles
blurb: The Victorian classic of self-improvement: lives of inventors, potters, artists, engineers and men of business, on perseverance, energy, the use of money, self-culture and character.

title: The Book of Household Management
author: Isabella Beeton
blurb: Mrs. Beeton's Victorian household manual: recipes with their costs and seasons, the natural history of foods, bills of fare, and chapters on servants, children, the doctor and the law.

title: Character Building: Being Addresses Delivered on Sunday Evenings to the Students of Tuskegee Institute
author: Booker T. Washington
blurb: Thirty-seven of the Sunday evening talks Booker T. Washington gave to Tuskegee students, on thrift, honesty, home-making, work on the land, simplicity, service and the future of the race.

title: Working with the Hands: Being a Sequel to "Up from Slavery," Covering the Author's Experiences in Industrial Training at Tuskegee
author: Booker T. Washington
blurb: Booker T. Washington describes industrial training at Tuskegee: its farms, shops and household arts, how students work their way through school, and what its graduates achieve.

title: Tuskegee & Its People: Their Ideals and Achievements
author: Booker T. Washington (ed.)
blurb: Tuskegee's officers and Hampton's Robert R. Moton describe the school and its teaching; seventeen graduates — farmer, carpenter, cooking teacher, druggist, blacksmith, lawyer and others — tell their stories.

title: How to Live on Twenty-Four Hours a Day
short: How to Live on Twenty-Four Hours a Day
author: Arnold Bennett
blurb: Arnold Bennett's brisk advice to the office worker on using the hours outside work: rising early, training the mind, reading seriously, the arts, and not overdoing the programme.

title: Good Things to Eat, as Suggested by Rufus: A Collection of Practical Recipes for Preparing Meats, Game, Fowl, Fish, Puddings, Pastries, Etc.
author: Rufus Estes
blurb: Rufus Estes, born in slavery in Tennessee and long a chef in Pullman private-car service, gives a sketch of his life and some six hundred recipes, soups to beverages.

title: Farmers of Forty Centuries; or, Permanent Agriculture in China, Korea and Japan
author: F. H. King
blurb: An American soil scientist travels through Japan, China and Korea in 1909, recording how farmers there kept their fields fertile for forty centuries through composting, irrigation and careful labor.

title: The Colored Girl Beautiful
author: E. Azalia Hackley
blurb: Talks to girls in Black boarding schools by the singer and teacher E. Azalia Hackley, on beauty, health, breathing, self-control, love, work, religion, home and motherhood.
